title: Why Sunlight Makes You Sneeze
sources: PBS NewsHour: Does the sun make you sneeze? (photic sneeze reflex, 10 to 35 percent of people, mechanism unclear)
Cleveland Clinic: Why does bright light make me sneeze (18 to 35 percent, crossed nerve signals theory, harmless)
ScienceBlog / PubMed 27568353 review: prevalence estimates, optic-trigeminal theories not confirmed, family and genome studies

lines.text: Why do you sneeze when you walk into bright sunlight?
If you do, you're not weird. Studies say up to one in three people do it!
It even has a name: the photic sneeze reflex.
Here's the weird part. Your eyes and your nose share nerve neighbours.
One leading theory is crossed wires: a flash of light sets off the nerve that senses an itchy nose,
so your brain thinks something is tickling your nose,
And the twist? Scientists still haven't proven exactly how it works.
It often runs in families, and it's harmless.
Next time you step into the sun, count your sneezes!
